outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a fictitious business name statement with the County Clerk. What to say: Register for a Business Registration Certificate online with the Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k). File the fictitious business name (DBA) statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail, then publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. The Business Account Number (BAN) from the registration is required for every other city permit.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,150 to $453,150. Notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and government cost of $3,150–$453,150 are for the Conditional Use Authorization and the ABC Type 47 premises-to-premises transfer when both are approved. The CUA accounts for 120–180 days and approximately $3,150 in application fees (CPI-adjusted, with possible First Year Free waiver). The ABC transfer accounts for 90–180 days and $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees, plus the market price of the Type 47 license itself ($100,000–$450,000 in San Francisco). The health permit (14–45 days, $470) is in parallel with the ABC investigation and does not extend the critical path. Protests, a public convenience or necessity hearing, or undue-concentration review can add 1–3 months to the ABC timeline. This range does not include the time or cost of building work, sign permits, or business formation, which are not entitlement approvals. It is a time to approval, not a time to denial or withdrawal.
